findings.issue: These files contain chapter milestones like <tei:milestone unit="chapter" n="30"/>, which carry @n but no @corresp. Under URN-scope rule 3, any milestone with a unit and no corresp is a terminator, so these open no chapter scope and their @n means nothing. The guideline also says bare terminators carry no @n. In qorbanot_qetoret.xml the chapter-n=30 + verse + bare verse + bare chapter group is repeated five times. These milestones are harmless to resolution, because a bare chapter milestone does not close verses (the unit must match exactly). They are still non-standard.
findings.action: If this is not an established house convention from earlier installments, drop the n-bearing chapter milestones that have no corresp, or use edition-verse-style display units. In qetoret, only the explicit terminator before וְנֶאֱמַר and at the end is needed, since adjacent verses 34–36 share boundaries. Not blocking.

findings.issue: In each project, the morning Shema repeats the verse milestone urn:x-opensiddur:text:bible:deuteronomy/6/4, which the evening Shema already uses. Per the Versification rules, the refdb and parallel compiler keep the first occurrence and warn. This is the intended design: the printing differs, and the expanded edition selects the structural morning URN. It is listed only so that the expected warning is not mistaken for a regression.
findings.action: None. Optionally note the expected duplicate-verse warning in the README or resolutions.

findings.issue: Page 9 prints one citation line, 'שמות ל׳. ויקרא ו׳.' (both readers' kiyyor_citation block). The encoding splits it into two standoff notes: 'שמות ל׳.' targets qorbanot/kiyyor and 'ויקרא ו׳.' targets leviticus/6/3. The text is exact and no outer parentheses are added, but 'ויקרא ו׳.' will now render at Lev 6:3 rather than on the shared line at the head of the page. Neither resolutions.json nor the enlarged decisions record this split.
findings.action: Accept the split as a deliberate per-passage attribution and record it in resolutions.json, or keep one note targeting the start of kiyyor. The text itself needs no change.

The adjudication of Name’s versus Name's in s53 is not recorded anywhere. All the adopted readings are image-based and the XML matches them. Only the cross-reference in the formal record is missing.
findings.action: List these in resolutions.json 'settled', pointing to the evidence in enlarged.json, or mark the comparison verdicts. Record the apostrophe choice (the XML uses ’).

alignment_findings.detail: Both sides have the div corresp siddur:rosh_hashanah/morning_blessings/lefikhakh, the prayer-part milestones prayer:lefikhakh and prayer:lefikhakh/ashreinu, and a closing bare prayer-part terminator. Hebrew ashreinu opens at 'אַשְׁרֵינוּ שֶׁאֲנַחְנוּ'; English opens at 'Fortunate are we that early and late'. These match. Each side keeps its printed paragraph.

Both sides have prayer-part attah_hu/ad_shelo, then attah_hu/uvishuatekha, then a terminator. Hebrew splits at 'וּבִישׁוּעָתְךָ'; English at 'and through Thy salvation'. These match. The file idno range ad_shelo-/uvishuatekha uses the correct absolute range form.

Both sides have the div corresp prayer:attah_hu/bashamayim and a bounded Zephaniah 3:20 verse milestone plus seg source, with an explicit verse terminator before the closing. Zeph 3:20 is printed in full on both sides, with no fabricated citation note. English keeps sic 'Thou has' and corr 'Thou hast'.

Both projects use the same structural div URNs. The Deut 6:4 milestone appears on both sides (see F2). Barukh Shem in each language is an inline transclusion of that project's own earlier witness, which is correct: no cross-language or cross-witness filling.
morning_qorbanot and its six modules exist only in the Hebrew project. No English file, transclusion or substitute translation was added.

Hebrew p8 is pb n=8 at n51.jpg (scan52) and English p8 is pb n=8 at n52.jpg (scan53). pb n=9 at n53.jpg is in kiyyor. pb n=10 at n54.jpg falls between 'אֶחָ֖ד' and 'תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה' inside Num 28:4, with one verse milestone, as required.

order_findings.detail: Expanded index lines 1341→1385: aval_anachnu → section_morning_prelude_continued (lefikhakh→ashreinu, the structural morning Shema, barukh_shem, ad_shelo→uvishuatekha, bashamayim) → section_morning_torah_german_later (german=true) → section_morning_qorbanot (kiyyor, Lev 6:3–4, tamid, veshachat, qorbanot/attah_hu, qetoret) → barukh_sheamar. This matches the requested sequence.
Other rites (german=false): the whole Torah/study block (lines 1251–1270) comes after asher_yatzar and before elohai_neshamah (1271–1286). The German Neshamah comes directly after asher_yatzar.

Morning Shema targets the edition-independent structural URN siddur:rosh_hashanah/morning_blessings/shema_yisrael, not bare bible:deuteronomy/6/4, so the evening witness cannot be picked up. barukh_shem intentionally uses the bare canonical URN.

The expanded edition has no page-turn or later-German navigation instruction. In both edition files, morning_blessings.xml:96 keeps the custom wording at the true end of p8, with only '(page …)' wrapped in seg type=optional-page-reference, a tei:ref type=page to birkhot_hatorah/laasoq in the same project, and the outer parentheses kept as printed. The Hebrew-page direction is printed in English, which is correct per the enlarged reading.

Qetoret runs Exod 30:34, 35, 36, then 'וְנֶאֱמַר' outside every verse scope, then 30:7, 30:8. No 30:37–38. The qetoret preface 'אַתָּה הוּא … כַּכָּתוּב בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ.' is encoded as a prayer tei:p, not an instruction.
None of the reused word modules gained a conditional. The offerings section is unconditional within the shaharit gate, which is correct for all rites.
